First, we substitute $u={x}^{7}-3.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=7{x}^{6}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=7{x}^{6}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{7}-3$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $-\infty $ | $-1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-\infty $ | $-4$ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{7{x}^{6}}{({x}^{7}-3)^{2}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{-4}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-4}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-4}{u}^{-2}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-{u}^{-1}]}_{a}^{-4} \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{u}]}_{a}^{-4} \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-4)}-\frac{1}{a}] \\  & =-(-\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
